thread:
mara.sec: FYI: new org policy rolling out for SSH key hygiene and privileged account review. Effective 2026-08-01 well require all human SSH keys used for access to prod systems to be short-lived (max 90d) and centrally-registered. Non-compliant keys will be disabled by the access proxy.

mara.sec: Why: we saw a few stale keys tied to former contractors during our audit last quarter. This reduces standing access and speeds offboarding.

mara.sec: Timeline: announcement now; discovery phase = two weeks; remediation window = 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-31; enforcement = 2026-08-01.

mara.sec: Steps for teams:
- Run `ssh-keyscan` / inventory script (we'll publish) to list keys registered to your services.
- Ensure keys are uploaded to our central key registry with an owner and expiry tag.
- Rotate or remove keys older than 90 days.

infra-bot: automated-scan: found 73 keys on prod jumpboxes with no expiry metadata, 12 keys owned by `unknown` accounts. Report posted to #security-scans.

jon.dev: For CI runners that use deploy keys (git-checkout), do we enforce expiry there too?

mara.sec: Yes, deploy keys are included. Prefer ephemeral deploy tokens from token-broker or GitHub deploy keys with expiration. If you need longer TTLs, file an exception with a justification and owner.

sam.sre: We'll prioritize jumpboxes and bastions first. Can infra-bot open tickets for owners automatically?

infra-bot: I can create tickets for keys that map cleanly to git/email. For unknown owners, I'll create a triage ticket assigned to SRE oncall.

lina.cto: Thanks for handling this. Heads-up to engineering leads: escalations for delayed remediation will go to managers after 2026-07-25.

mara.sec: We'll publish the inventory script, runbook, and registry link by EOD. If you need help mapping keys to owners, ping me or open a ticket labeled `sec-ssh-hygiene`.

jon.dev: Noted. I'll run the inventory against our services this weekend and tag owners in the PRs.

mara.sec: Appreciate it. Reminder: enforcement 2026-08-01. Old/no-expiry keys will be disabled at the proxy level.
